The video segment shows a man on a baseball field, sitting on a bag, who introduces himself as the owner, editor, and producer of Baseball Bat Bros. He is wearing a black shirt with the text “WHATUP WHATUP” (What’s up? What’s up?), a black cap with a yellow “P” on it, and black pants. He says that he’ll be showing what’s in his baseball bag and holds two baseball bats in his hands as the camera pans out to show his full body. There is baseball field with yellow ropes around it behind him. There is a cut and a glitching effect before the title card appears with text that reads, “What’s In My Baseball Bag? Ft. Will Taylor from the Baseball Bat Bros.” Then, he continues talking about his bats, picking up a black baseball bat, and showing its unique features and mentioning other bats. He is smiling and friendly. Overall, the setting is bright and outdoors on the baseball field.

The video shows a baseball field during the daytime with clear weather. A man wearing a Pittsburgh Pirates baseball cap and a black long-sleeved shirt with "WHATUP WHATUP Baseball" written on it sits cross-legged on a backpack on the field. He is holding two wooden baseball bats, presenting them to the camera. The man smiles, gestures with the bats, and speaks enthusiastically. One bat, with a brown finish, is labeled "Batsmith Riverton, Utah" and "Professional Maple Will Taylor." The other bat has an orange finish. The camera zooms in on the bats on the grass, showing their details. There are overlay effects used to transition, such as light beams and transparent bat overlays. He also states the drop of each bat, one being a drop 2.75, basically a drop 3, while the other is a drop 2. The man believes his favorite grip and handle is the no knob.

In an outdoor setting, a man is seen on a baseball field. He's wearing a "P" baseball cap, a black long-sleeved shirt with text that reads "WHATUP WHATUP" and "Baseball" printed across it, black pants, and black sneakers. The man is sitting atop a large black tire and holding a blue and white backpack with an American flag patch. He indicates that the backpack is a DeMarini brand and that it can hold six bats, but that it's starting to tear. He proceeds to state that he will show us what is inside and that he likes to prepare in case they shoot up to 4 videos a day. Three baseball bats are lying on the field to the right of him. The background reveals a green building labeled "WEST LINN BASEBALL" in white letters. Red baseball lines are marked in the grass on the field. The camera angle remains mostly static throughout the segment, with slight adjustments to keep the man in focus as he moves his body and gestures to the backpack.

The video segment features a man wearing a "WHATUP WHATUP" shirt and a baseball cap with a "P" logo, seated on a black backpack on a baseball field. He's holding two yellow baseball gloves, the gloves are branded "WARSTIC", and says they're "Workman 3" brand, before putting them down on the grass. The camera zooms in on the gloves, revealing that one glove has the text "BAT" across its yellow wrist strap, while the other says "TLE". He then tries on one of the gloves and smiles, before placing the pair of gloves by his bag. Then, he pulls out a pair of white baseball gloves, which also have a wrist strap. After this, the camera zooms in on the white gloves, which have the text "STINGER" on them. He states that the batting gloves are also backups. Beside him on the grass are four baseball bats of varying colors. The background shows the baseball field, a building with the words "West Linn Baseball," a chain-link fence, and trees. There are brief transitions that overlay images of the gloves on top of the seated man.

The video segment shows a man on a baseball field sitting on his black backpack, surrounded by baseball bats. He is wearing a black shirt with white text "WHATUP WHATUP Baseball" on it. He also wears black pants, a red-black baseball cap, and black sneakers. He is showing a pair of white and grey batting gloves, with the text "TRUE" and "RUB" on them. He mentions that these are his go-to batting gloves, and that they have a palm pad, which he likes. He takes the gloves and puts them in his bag. The next thing he holds up is a pair of white pro-hitter rings, with text "PRO-HITTER" inscribed. The background consists of a baseball field with artificial green turf, a red running path, a fence and a green building with the text "West Linn Baseball" on it. The camera zooms in on the batting gloves and the pro-hitter rings to provide a clearer view of the objects.

The video segment features a man sitting outdoors on a black bag in front of a baseball field. He is wearing a black long-sleeve shirt that says "WHATUP WHATUP Baseball" in white text, black pants, and a black and red baseball cap with the letter “P” on it. Throughout the segment, the man is pulling items out of his bag to show to the audience. The first item the man is holding up is what he describes as “fancy microphone” that he uses to prevent wind. He then promotes a fanny pack on the brand website, baseballbatbros.com. Next, the man talks about “Pelican” bat wax, or “Pine Stick”, that he says he prefers to “Tiger Stick” for the stickiness. He opens the wax, says it smells nice, and says it is his favorite kind of pine tar. He moves on to bat grips, showing two different brands, VukGripz and Vulcan. Lastly, he shows a black “Pocket Radar” velocity tester that he says he uses to test velocity off the tee or the mound. The baseball field is green with a red dirt running track surrounding the field. There is a green building in the background and a brick building with yellow tape covering part of the building.

He holds up the empty bag to show that he is finished with the "What's In My Bag" segment of his show. He concludes the video sitting on the backpack, with the baseballs, glove, sneakers, and two baseball bats in front of him, all against the backdrop of a baseball field. The video begins with a man in a grey hooded sweatshirt and a black baseball cap standing on a wooden deck. He is looking at the camera and gesturing, speaking with a positive, friendly expression. Next to him is a screenshot of an Instagram post that reads “Shotbyhype Winston-Salem, North Carolina” and shows two pairs of athletic cleats. Text in the screenshot reads “WIN A FREE PAIR OF CLEATS, SUBSCRIBE TO THE YOUTUBE CHANNEL SHOTBYHYPE, FOLLOW @SHOTBYHYPE ON INSTAGRAM, COMMENT 2 FRIENDS BELOW, #SHOTBYHYPE5K” (to summarize, it provides instructions on how to enter a giveaway of athletic cleats). The camera view widens slightly as the man continues speaking. He points at the camera. The setting includes a backyard with trees, a wooden fence, an umbrella, and a small shed. Towards the video's end, there is a sudden transition where the screen turns completely red and then cuts to an end screen with a white backdrop and red accents with the text “Thanks for Watching, Follow Me On Instagram, Facebook, & Twitter” and icons to subscribe and view additional videos.
